note: City of Smithville, Bastrop County, TX. INSTRUMENT: the "Zoning Ordinance of the City of Smithville, Texas" (Sec. 1.1, title), adopted as Ordinance 2018-555 on October 16, 2018 and included as Exhibit A to Chapter 14 of the City of Smithville Code of Ordinances, as amended -- Code Sec. 14.02.001 states verbatim: "The zoning ordinance, Ordinance 2018-555, adopted by the city on October 16, 2018, as amended, is included at the end of this chapter as exhibit A." Sec. 1.2 (Effective Date) reads: "This Ordinance shall become effective immediately upon its passage and publication, as the law in such cases provides, and it is accordingly so ordained." Sec. 1.3 amends and reenacts the prior zoning code "in its entirety, replacing all prior provisions with the provisions herein," so there is no retired scheme to lift rows from -- every row here is from the in-force text. effectiveDate is the 2018-10-16 adoption. eCODE360 SCRAPE RULING (doc_repo _decisions/2026-08-04_ecode360_partnership_retired_scrape_posture.md: zoning is public record, acquired by scraping; the ruling's own words name the proof target as proving the ecode360-scraper adapter or the citizen-portal path, whichever lands the corpus). SATISFIED, and with a live re-verification rather than only the prior proof: this lane re-fetched https://ecode360.com/39658868 on 2026-09-16 with User-Agent "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; PublicLawTextFetcher/1.0)" and got HTTP 200 with the full Sec. 2.2 text (the UA profile is the one the B1 proof recorded in P:/tmp/tx_scraper_proofs/smithville/STATUS.md -- robots.txt allows the numeric content paths and /SM6484, and a Chrome-UA "browser" profile gets a Cloudflare 403 challenge instead, which is why the plain-browser route is NOT the citation route). The extracted Sec. 2.2 paragraph sequence was then byte-compared against the same section in the 2026-07-30 B1 scrape artifact (normalized.json: sourceUrl https://ecode360.com/SM6484, fetchedAt 2026-07-30T03:36:52.351Z, eCode360-scraper adapter, 155 pages, custId SM6484): 676 paragraphs on each side, ONE difference, and it is an encoding artifact (the artifact stores ">65 ft from front property line" where the live HTML carries the entity >). The text coded here is therefore the same text the two routes independently return. No. 2025-689 adopted July 14, 2025." The July 2026 scrape metadata records the same publicationDate 2025-07-14, so the scraped revision and the currently published revision agree; the rows below are the revision in force. The citation URL that reproduces them is the section route named above, not a bare URL: a plain fetch of https://ecode360.com/39658868 WITHOUT the UA profile does not return the text. SCOPE OF THIS TABLE: all 16 Euclidean districts whose dimension tables Sec. 2.2 states, numbered by their subsection in the ordinance (Sec. 2.1 fixes the district list, and the ORDER of the Sec. 2.2 subsections is confirmed independently by two self-references in the text itself -- Sec. 2.2.11 is the CBD and Sec. 2.2.15 is the CF district, which match the 11th and 15th subsections below): SF-1 (2.2.1), SF-2 (2.2.2), TH (2.2.3), MF (2.2.4), MH (2.2.5), MHS (2.2.6), MR (2.2.7), C-1 (2.2.8), C-2 (2.2.9), C-3 (2.2.10), CBD (2.2.11), RVP (2.2.12), I (2.2.13), P (2.2.14), CF (2.2.15), PD-Z (2.2.17). NOT CODED, deliberately: PDD (2.2.16) is a planned development district whose standards are set by the individual development plan and the ordinance establishing it, not by a district schedule -- it routes to the PUD refusal, and asserting a row for it would invent a standard the code does not state; HD (2.2.18) and HCD (2.2.19) are overlay districts layered on a base district with no independent dimensional schedule (their text regulates certificates of appropriateness, prohibited uses and design standards, not yards or height). READING RULES APPLIED. (1) Where a dimension states a base case plus a conditional one, the BASE case is coded and the condition is preserved verbatim in the quote: SF-1/SF-2 rear = 20 ft ("or 20% of lot depth", the smaller governs); SF-1/SF-2 side = the one-story figure (7-1/2 ft and 5 ft respectively) with the over-one-story figure (10 ft) in the quote; MHS and MR corner-side = 25 ft ("25 feet for all other conditions" with 15 ft only when backing onto/abutting another corner lot) whereas SF-1 and SF-2 corner-side = 15 ft ("25 feet when abutting another corner lot"); C-1/C-2/C-3 side 10 ft and rear 10 ft; MF rear = 25 ft with the 50-ft parking-and-adjacency condition quoted. (2) MH's yard figures are alternative site conditions rather than a single scalar (25 ft fronting a public street vs 10 ft fronting an internal private street; 15 ft if the home is centered on the lot vs 30 ft if it sits on a lot line; 25 ft rear abutting a public street vs 10 ft abutting a private street): the public-street/centered case is coded and the alternative is quoted, at reduced confidence 0.75, because a MH-park parcel's answer depends on the site plan, not on the district alone. (3) PD-Z's side standard is stated COMBINED -- "Minimum combined side yard setback for both attached units: 15 feet" -- which is not a per-side scalar, so side_ft is coded not_specified with the combined figure quoted rather than halved or guessed. (4) Districts that state no yard standard at all (I, P) are not_specified, not 0: their dimension rows simply omit yards, and this lane will not read silence as a permissive zero. CBD is different and IS coded 0 for front and side because the ordinance says so affirmatively: "Front yard setback: Not required" / "Side yard setback: Not required." (5) No district in Sec. 2.2 states an impervious-surface standard distinct from lot coverage, so max_impervious_pct is not_specified for all 16 rows; several districts state no lot-coverage cap either, and those rows are not_specified for max_lot_coverage_pct too, with the district's actual dimension-row list quoted so the absence is checkable. COVERAGE BASIS: the P-255 census's no-table city rows carry no per-district stamp breakdown, so this table was checked against the ordinance's own district list (Sec. 2.1) and every dimensional district in it has a row except the planned-development and overlay districts named above. The live GIS stamp vocabulary for Smithville could NOT be re-read in this pass (no staged layer for this city and no district list in the census row); that check is left open rather than assumed. SENTINELS: not_specified fields carry 100, the Belton/ldt fan-out convention, EXCEPT max_height_ft, which carries the corpus gate's G7 canonical 999 where a district states no height at all (no Smithville district here needed it -- every coded district states a height, and the not_specified height count in this table is zero). No value in this table is a converted or interpolated number; every quoted number is the ordinance's own.
